evidence.observation: H701 reads 389.506 °C, markedly discordant with H702 at 83.049 °C and reboiler liquid at 72.663 °C.
H701 has risen to 395.350 °C while H702 is 83.348 °C and reboiler liquid is 73.048 °C; the persistent disparity suggests a heater or temperature-measurement anomaly, but does not identify its cause.

System pressure is 499.516 mbar, column differential pressure 0.576 mbar, upper-column temperatures approximately 63.3–63.4 °C, and cooling flow 3.646; these do not show a corresponding broad thermal or pressure excursion.
Distillate flow is 0.004 and reflux flow 0.780; without flow targets or collection-cycle information these do not independently establish a fault.

args.missing_evidence: H701 operating setpoint and allowable heater-surface temperature, heater power/readback, and an independent temperature check are needed to distinguish genuine overheating from sensor bias or drift. Composition measurement and target specification are needed to assess separation.
